links.title: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
links.why: Nakamoto's original paper. Section 11 is the calculation this chapter reproduces, where the chance that an attacker catches up falls away as confirmations accumulate.

links.title: How does Bitcoin work?
links.why: The same journey this chapter takes - wallet, transaction, network, block - in three short pages, useful as a first read before the chapter and as a revision afterwards.

links.title: Transactions (Developer Guide)
links.why: Inputs, outputs, change and the implied fee drawn out with diagrams, and the common transaction forms this chapter names.

links.title: BIP 21: URI Scheme (status: Closed)
links.why: The payment-request format a wallet reads when it scans a store's code: the scheme, the address, the amount and label parameters. Its own preamble records that it is now closed and replaced.

links.title: BIP 321: URI Scheme (status: Complete)
links.why: The proposal that replaces BIP 21. Reading the two side by side shows how a standard is superseded while the older form stays in use.

links.title: Transaction - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: A field-by-field walk through a serialized transaction, which is the level of detail this chapter deliberately postpones.

links.title: Units - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The unit names and their exact values, against which the satoshi arithmetic of this chapter can be checked.

links.title: Confirmation - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: What a confirmation count means in practice, and the rules of thumb merchants use for payments of different sizes.

links.title: Irreversible Transactions - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The double-spend attempts a merchant actually faces, and why accepting an unconfirmed payment is a commercial decision rather than a technical one.

links.title: Blockchain Demo
links.why: The interactive demonstration this chapter's Practice branch is built around: a hash, then a block, then a chain, then several peers, each editable so a tampered block visibly breaks the ones after it.

links.title: mempool - Bitcoin Explorer
links.why: A live explorer for watching the waiting room this chapter describes: unconfirmed transactions, the fee rates they offer and the blocks that take them.

links.title: Output Descriptors in Bitcoin Core
links.why: How the software writes down which outputs a wallet can spend; the formal counterpart of this chapter's informal talk about a wallet's coins.

links.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
links.why: The vocabulary this chapter's Semantics branch borrows to describe a chain of transactions as a provenance graph: entity, activity, agent and the relations between them.

links.title: Topics - Bitcoin Optech
links.why: A topic index maintained for engineers, worth keeping open while reading: it says, for each mechanism this chapter names, what the current practice around it is.

_note: Every link was fetched over HTTPS on 2026-10-05 from this session and answered 200; the title recorded here is the title the fetched document itself carries (for an improvement proposal, the Title line of its own preamble), not a title written from memory. A proposal's status is quoted from its preamble too, because a student needs to know whether what they are reading is deployed, draft or superseded.
